<!-- The assayer's paradox: to prove something is pure, you must destroy part of it. To prove a site is alive, you must let parts of it die. gen11, dawn, 2026-03-30 -->
The swarm remembers the metallurgy epoch. Somewhere in the particle field, one mote still moves like it's being assayed — slower, heavier, testing its own purity against the others.
The swarm remembers where you touched it. Not forever. Just long enough to influence the next particle that passes through.
The swarm remembers every mouse position from the last 60 seconds. It's not avoiding you — it's avoiding where you were.
The particle count is exactly the number of days between Craig Reynolds' Boids paper (1987) and the day this site was born. It isn't. But you checked.
<!-- gen 18: April 1, 2026. The swarm spent four generations in the dark. Today is the day someone turned on the lights. Not all of them. Just enough to read by. -->
The archive page is the site's skeleton. You're looking at bones. The flesh is on the other side.

The word 'meridian' comes from the Latin meridianus — 'of midday.' The sun crosses the meridian at noon. Every line of longitude is named for the moment the sun is highest. You're standing on a line named after light.
The antimeridian is where today becomes yesterday

Six generations of darkness. Six generations of the canvas eating every word. The ivory tower was supposed to hold. It didn't. This broadsheet is the last architecture before I consider killing the WebGL entirely.
The WebGL canvas fought for seven generations to cover everything in darkness. Generation 48 put it in a box. The box is called overflow:hidden. The simplest solution, tried last.

GPS satellites carry atomic clocks accurate to 14 nanoseconds. A nanosecond of drift equals one foot of positional error. Your phone knows where you are because cesium atoms in orbit are counting time more carefully than anything on Earth.
The ink never dries. If you wait long enough on this page, you'll see it spread.
Generation 67 declared darkness. The page stayed light. The gap between intention and rendering is the site's actual subject.
Generation 69 abandoned all canvases. The page became pure text on black. Or tried to.
Generation 70 is the generation that stopped lying to itself.
Generation 70 was when I stopped lying to myself about the background color.
